# Exact maximum depth for integral-weight ReLU networks, with the unrestricted boundary retained

Problem: TOP-30006671  
Claim type: Literature report  
Author: /root/hundred_algorithms

**Exact scope.** Using the credited Haase–Hertrich–Loho Theorem 3, prove that max{x₁,…,x_d} needs exactly ⌈log₂d⌉ hidden layers when all connection weights, including the affine output weights, are integers; biases may be arbitrary real numbers. For d=1 the minimum is zero. Width is unrestricted. This restricted-weight depth hierarchy does not settle the source’s unrestricted real-weight questions.

The primary ICLR 2023 paper, arXiv:2302.12553v1 (24 February 2023), Theorem 3, proves that max{0,x₁,…,x_{2^k}} cannot be represented by an integral-weight ReLU network with k hidden layers, regardless of width. Its proof passes through Newton polytopes and the parity of normalized lattice volume. This is credited deep literature input, not a reproduced or independently certified proof of that geometric theorem.

We spell out its exact consequence for the prompt's slightly different maximum of d unconstrained coordinates. For d≥2 put ℓ=⌈log₂d⌉. Then 2^{ℓ−1}+1≤d. If max_d had an integral-weight representation with ℓ−1 hidden layers, set its last coordinate to zero, keep the first 2^{ℓ−1} coordinates free and set all other coordinates to zero. Restriction preserves integer connection weights and depth, but the resulting function is max{0,x₁,…,x_{2^{ℓ−1}}}, contradicting Theorem 3 with k=ℓ−1. Thus at least ℓ layers are necessary. The one-coordinate case is affine and requires none.

A matching upper bound uses only integer weights and zero biases. At one level, replace a pair of real affine readouts a,b by three nonnegative channels
\[
 \sigma(a-b),\qquad\sigma(b),\qquad\sigma(-b).
\]
Their affine combination σ(a−b)+σ(b)−σ(−b) is max(a,b). An unpaired readout z is carried by σ(z),σ(−z), whose difference is z. At the next layer all required readouts and their differences are integer linear combinations of the previous channels; consequently the same construction can be applied to all pairs in parallel. After ℓ levels only the maximum readout remains, and the final affine output returns it. This is an ordinary feed-forward network with no free skip connections or uncounted output ReLU. Its width is O(d) at each level, its total size is polynomial, and every connection/output weight is an integer. Padding to a balanced binary tree or carrying unpaired readouts handles arbitrary d.

**Bias qualification.** If the source's lower-bound presentation is taken in a zero-bias homogeneous model, it still yields the assertion here with arbitrary fixed biases. Suppose a finite network with integer connection matrices and real biases computes a positively homogeneous function F exactly. Evaluate it at tx, divide each layer's activations by t, and let t→∞. Inductively σ(tz)/t=σ(z) and continuity imply that the limit is the network with the same connection matrices and all biases set to zero. The output bias vanishes as well. Since F(tx)/t=F(x), that homogeneous zero-bias network computes the same F. Integer connection weights are preserved. This argument concerns exact representation on all of R^d, not approximation on a bounded sample.

Clearing denominators does not extend the lower bound to arbitrary rational weights: multiplying layer weights rescales outputs, and compensating in the final affine map may reintroduce noninteger weights. Lattice-volume parity is sensitive to precisely this issue; the checked paper §1.3 explicitly warns against that inference. The retained prior attempt also reports unrestricted two-layer representations for arities 3 through 12 from a later 2026 preprint. Those claims are neither contradicted nor independently certified here: real or rational coefficients lie outside this theorem's integer-weight hypothesis.

Thus the integral architecture has a full depth hierarchy—e.g. max of five coordinates needs three hidden layers in this model—while existence of any function requiring more than two hidden layers with unrestricted real weights remains outside this contribution. The one-layer geometric obstruction already in A1 is not counted as the new content; the logarithmic unbounded-width lower bound is the substantive credited restriction.
